title: Zero-Downtime RollingUpdate Deployment with Graceful Shutdown & Probes
whatThisCodeCovers: A production-grade Deployment manifest featuring 25% rolling update limits, startup/readiness/liveness probes, and preStop sleep hooks to prevent dropped in-flight HTTP connections during pod termination.
code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-api
  namespace: production
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: payment-api
spec:
  replicas: 4
  revisionHistoryLimit: 10
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%        # Spin up 1 extra pod before killing old ones
      maxUnavailable: 0     # Ensure 100% target capacity during rollout
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payment-api
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60
      containers:
      - name: payment-api
        image: registry.example.com/finance/payment-api:v2.4.0
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              # Give kube-proxy / ingress controllers 15s to remove pod from endpoints
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 15"]
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
          name: http
        startupProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz/startup
            port: http
          failureThreshold: 30
          periodSeconds: 2 # Up to 60s warm up
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz/ready
            port: http
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
          timeoutSeconds: 2
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz/live
            port: http
          periodSeconds: 10
          failureThreshold: 3
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 512Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 1000m
            memory: 1024Mi
breakdown: Sets maxUnavailable to 0 ensuring full throughput throughout updates. PreStop hook executes a 15-second sleep, providing ample propagation time for endpoints controllers to sever inbound traffic before the application process receives SIGTERM.
expectedOutput: Zero dropped HTTP requests during rolling updates, with graceful TCP connection drainage and automatic rollback on probe failures.

title: Production StatefulSet with Headless Service & VolumeClaimTemplates
whatThisCodeCovers: A clustered stateful deployment (PostgreSQL/Kafka style) using StatefulSets, dedicated Headless Service DNS routing, and per-pod dynamic PersistentVolumeClaim storage templates.
code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: postgres-cluster-headless
  namespace: databases
  labels:
    app: postgres-cluster
spec:
  clusterIP: None # Headless service for direct DNS routing
  ports:
  - port: 5432
    name: postgresql
  selector:
    app: postgres-cluster
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: postgres-node
  namespace: databases
spec:
  serviceName: "postgres-cluster-headless"
  replicas: 3
  podManagementPolicy: OrderedReady
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: postgres-cluster
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: postgres-cluster
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - labelSelector:
              matchExpressions:
              - key: app
                operator: In
                values: ["postgres-cluster"]
            topologyKey: "kubernetes.io/hostname" # Strict one pod per node
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: postgres:15.4-alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 5432
          name: postgresql
        volumeMounts:
        - name: pgdata
          mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: pgdata
    spec:
      accessModes: [ "ReadWriteOnce" ]
      storageClassName: "gp3-ebs"
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 100Gi
breakdown: Combines a headless service with volumeClaimTemplates so each replica gets a dedicated, isolated cloud block volume (pgdata-postgres-node-0, 1, 2) and deterministic DNS hostname.
expectedOutput: Stable ordinal pods postgres-node-0, postgres-node-1, postgres-node-2 each retaining their attached 100Gi EBS volumes across pod restarts.

title: High-Throughput Ingress with TLS Termination, Path Routing & Rate Limiting
whatThisCodeCovers: An enterprise NGINX Ingress manifest routing traffic across microservices, terminating TLS using Cert-Manager certificates, and enforcing rate limiting.
code:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: enterprise-api-gateway
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: "nginx"
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: "letsencrypt-prod"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/backend-protocol: "HTTP"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "100"           # 100 req/sec rate limit per client IP
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst-multiplier: "3" # Burst factor
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "60"
spec:
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - api.company.com
    secretName: api-company-tls-cert
  rules:
  - host: api.company.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /v1/orders
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: order-service
            port:
              number: 8080
      - path: /v1/payments
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: payment-service
            port:
              number: 8080
breakdown: Defines path-based layer 7 routing under a single TLS-secured domain, enforcing strict TLS redirection and automated SSL certificate management with NGINX rate-limiting.
expectedOutput: Secure HTTPS endpoints on api.company.com routing /v1/orders and /v1/payments with automatic HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect and 100 req/s rate limits.

title: Dynamic Persistent Volume Provisioning with WaitForFirstConsumer
whatThisCodeCovers: A cloud-agnostic StorageClass and PersistentVolumeClaim configuration enforcing delayed volume binding until pod scheduling, preventing Availability Zone mismatches.
code:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: high-performance-ssd
provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer # Delay creation until Pod is placed on a node!
allowVolumeExpansion: true              # Permit dynamic disk size increase
reclaimPolicy: Delete
parameters:
  type: gp3
  iops: "3000"
  throughput: "125"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: elasticsearch-data-pvc
  namespace: logging
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: high-performance-ssd
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 250Gi
breakdown: WaitForFirstConsumer halts dynamic volume creation until the scheduler assigns the consumer pod to a specific node, ensuring the cloud block volume is provisioned in the exact same Availability Zone.
expectedOutput: PVC status remains 'Pending' until a consuming pod is scheduled, at which point the 250Gi gp3 volume is provisioned in the correct zone and transitions to 'Bound'.

title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA v2) with Multi-Metric Scaling
whatThisCodeCovers: An HPA v2 manifest scaling a deployment based on both average CPU utilization (70%) and a custom Prometheus business metric (HTTP request rate of 1500 req/sec).
code:
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: checkout-scaler
  namespace: production
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: checkout-service
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 30
  metrics:
  # Metric 1: System Resource (CPU)
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70
  # Metric 2: Application Throughput (Prometheus Custom Metric)
  - type: Pods
    pods:
      metric:
        name: http_requests_per_second
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: 1500m # 1.5 requests/sec per pod
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300 # Prevent premature flapping
      policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 10
        periodSeconds: 60
breakdown: HPA calculates target replicas across both metrics and selects the maximum replica count, ensuring capacity spikes during CPU-intensive tasks or high-throughput request floods.
expectedOutput: Automated scaling between 3 and 30 replicas with a 5-minute cooldown stabilization window dampening downscaling spikes.

title: Pod Topology Spread Constraints across Multi-Zone Availability Domains
whatThisCodeCovers: Production topology spread configuration ensuring application pods are evenly distributed across cloud Availability Zones with maxSkew=1.
code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: auth-service
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 6
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: auth-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: auth-service
    spec:
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      # 1. Distribute across Availability Zones
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule # Hard enforcement
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: auth-service
      # 2. Distribute across physical Nodes within zones
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
        whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway # Soft preference
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: auth-service
      containers:
      - name: auth-service
        image: auth-service:v1.0.0
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
breakdown: Restricts difference between any two zones to at most 1 replica. If an entire cloud zone experiences an outage, surviving zones maintain equal, redundant load distribution.
expectedOutput: 6 replicas scheduled as exactly 2 in us-east-1a, 2 in us-east-1b, and 2 in us-east-1c.

title: PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) Enforcing Minimum High-Availability
whatThisCodeCovers: A PodDisruptionBudget guaranteeing that automated node drains, cluster upgrades, and autoscaler consolidations cannot drop available replicas below safe thresholds.
code:
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: order-service-pdb
  namespace: production
spec:
  minAvailable: 80% # Guarantee at least 80% of desired pods remain ready
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: order-service
---
# Alternative PDB using absolute integer count
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: critical-redis-pdb
  namespace: caching
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 1 # At most 1 pod may be down during maintenance
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redis-sentinel
breakdown: When an engineer or automated agent issues 'kubectl drain', the Eviction API rejects eviction requests if the eviction would violate the PDB's minAvailable threshold.
expectedOutput: Cluster maintenance operations drain nodes one by one without breaching the 80% service availability guarantee.

title: Resilient CronJob with Forbid Concurrency & ActiveDeadlineSeconds
whatThisCodeCovers: A production batch CronJob configured to prevent overlapping job executions, enforce hard runtime timeouts, and limit history retention.
code:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: nightly-financial-ledger-sync
  namespace: finance
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *" # Every morning at 2:00 AM UTC
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid # Never start a new job if previous run is still active!
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 300
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 5
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 3600 # Hard kill if job runs > 1 hour
      backoffLimit: 3             # Retry failed pods at most 3 times
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
          - name: ledger-sync
            image: registry.example.com/finance/ledger-worker:latest
            command: ["npm", "run", "sync:ledger"]
            resources:
              requests:
                cpu: 500m
                memory: 1Gi
breakdown: concurrencyPolicy: Forbid prevents double-processing financial transactions if a job hangs. activeDeadlineSeconds terminates stalled batch runs after 1 hour.
expectedOutput: Reliable nightly execution with execution overlap prevention and automated pruning of old completed job pods.

title: InitContainers for Database Schema Migration & Service Wait Gates
whatThisCodeCovers: A Pod specification utilizing chained initContainers to wait for backend PostgreSQL connectivity and apply Liquibase/Flyway migrations before launching application containers.
code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: user-management-service
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: user-management
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: user-management
    spec:
      initContainers:
      # Init 1: Wait until PostgreSQL TCP port 5432 is responding
      - name: wait-for-postgres
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ['sh', '-c',
          'until nc -z -w 2 postgres-cluster.databases.svc.cluster.local 5432; do
             echo "Waiting for postgresql cluster...";
             sleep 2;
           done']
      # Init 2: Execute Liquibase / Prisma / TypeORM schema migration
      - name: db-migrate
        image: registry.example.com/apps/user-migration:v1.4.0
        command: ["npm", "run", "prisma:migrate:deploy"]
        env:
        - name: DATABASE_URL
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: db-credentials
              key: connection_string
      containers:
      - name: user-app
        image: registry.example.com/apps/user-api:v1.4.0
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
breakdown: Init containers execute sequentially to completion before main containers start. If migrations fail, the pod restarts the init container with backoff, preventing application crashes against unmigrated tables.
expectedOutput: Guaranteed sequential startup: connectivity check succeeds -> migration runs -> application server launches.

title: DaemonSet with HostPort & Tolerations for Cluster-Wide Telemetry
whatThisCodeCovers: A DaemonSet manifest deploying a node-level telemetry and security agent across every worker and master node using tolerations and host PID access.
code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: node-telemetry-agent
  namespace: monitoring
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: node-telemetry
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: node-telemetry
    spec:
      hostPID: true
      hostNetwork: true
      dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet
      tolerations:
      # Tolerate master / control-plane taints to monitor all nodes
      - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane
        operator: Exists
        effect: NoSchedule
      - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/master
        operator: Exists
        effect: NoSchedule
      containers:
      - name: agent
        image: agent/telemetry:v3.2.0
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
        volumeMounts:
        - name: proc
          mountPath: /host/proc
          readOnly: true
        - name: sys
          mountPath: /host/sys
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: proc
        hostPath:
          path: /proc
      - name: sys
        hostPath:
          path: /sys
breakdown: Deploys exactly 1 replica per node throughout the cluster. Tolerations allow scheduling onto tainted control-plane nodes, providing 100% cluster-wide telemetry coverage.
expectedOutput: Telemetry agents launched on every node in the cluster, including master nodes, continuously monitoring host /proc and /sys.

title: Granular Zero-Trust NetworkPolicy for Multi-Tier Microservice Isolation
whatThisCodeCovers: A multi-tier NetworkPolicy enforcing default-deny, allowing frontend-to-backend communication on port 8080, and strictly isolating database egress to port 5432 and CoreDNS on port 53.
code:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: backend-api-network-policy
  namespace: production
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: backend-api
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  ingress:
  # Allow Ingress ONLY from frontend pods on port 8080
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: frontend-ui
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
  egress:
  # 1. Allow Egress to Postgres database pods on port 5432
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: postgres-db
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 5432
  # 2. Allow Egress to CoreDNS pods in kube-system on port 53 (UDP & TCP)
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          k8s-app: kube-dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
breakdown: Enforces strict microservice segmentation. Lateral movement is completely blocked: even if backend-api is compromised, it cannot reach other namespaces or the public Internet.
expectedOutput: Backend API receives traffic strictly from Frontend UI, can only talk to PostgreSQL and CoreDNS, and rejects all other network communication.

title: Least-Privilege RBAC: ServiceAccount, Role & RoleBinding for CI/CD
whatThisCodeCovers: A scoped RBAC definition granting a CI/CD automation ServiceAccount permission to deploy and roll out updates within a single namespace without cluster admin rights.
code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: github-actions-deployer
  namespace: staging
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: deployment-manager
  namespace: staging
rules:
# 1. Manage Deployments and Rollouts
- apiGroups: ["apps"]
  resources: ["deployments", "replicasets"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "update", "patch"]
# 2. View Pods and Stream Logs
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods", "pods/log"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
# 3. Manage ConfigMaps for releases
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "update", "patch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: bind-deployer-role
  namespace: staging
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: github-actions-deployer
  namespace: staging
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: deployment-manager
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
breakdown: Confines the deployment pipeline strictly to the 'staging' namespace. Prevents destructive permissions like deleting namespaces or accessing secrets outside the project.
expectedOutput: The github-actions-deployer ServiceAccount can execute rolling updates and tail logs in 'staging' while being denied access to secrets and other namespaces.

title: ClusterRole & ClusterRoleBinding for Global Monitoring & Telemetry
whatThisCodeCovers: A cluster-wide ClusterRole granting Prometheus or Datadog collectors read-only visibility into Nodes, Services, Pods, and Endpoints across all namespaces.
code:
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: prometheus-cluster-reader
rules:
# 1. Core cluster resources
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources:
  - nodes
  - nodes/metrics
  - services
  - endpoints
  - pods
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
# 2. Non-resource metrics endpoints
- nonResourceURLs: ["/metrics", "/metrics/cadvisor"]
  verbs: ["get"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: prometheus-cluster-binding
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: prometheus-k8s
  namespace: monitoring
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: prometheus-cluster-reader
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
breakdown: Binds cluster-scoped read permissions without granting write/delete powers, allowing the monitoring stack to discover all pod endpoints globally.
expectedOutput: Prometheus ServiceAccount reads node metrics and watches pods globally without having privileges to alter or delete any cluster objects.

title: Enforcing Pod Security Standards 'Restricted' Profile
whatThisCodeCovers: A namespace labeled with PSA 'restricted' policy and a matching Pod SecurityContext that drops all Linux capabilities, runs as non-root, and mounts a read-only rootfs.
code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: secure-apps
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version: latest
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn: restricted
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: hardened-microservice
  namespace: secure-apps
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secure-app
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        runAsGroup: 10001
        fsGroup: 10001
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example.com/app:v1.0
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tmp-dir
          mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
      - name: tmp-dir
        emptyDir: {}
breakdown: Enforces zero-trust container sandboxing. If any container attempts privilege escalation or root execution, kube-apiserver rejects admission immediately.
expectedOutput: Deployment passes admission under strict 'restricted' PSA policy with read-only rootfs and no host capabilities.

title: External Secrets Operator (ESO) Syncing from AWS Secrets Manager

title: Live ConfigMap Mounting with Symlinks vs SubPath Invalidation
whatThisCodeCovers: A ConfigMap volume mount pattern demonstrating directory mounting for live in-memory configuration updates without container restarts.
code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-dynamic-config
  namespace: production
data:
  appsettings.json: |
    {
      "LogLevel": "Information",
      "FeatureFlag_NewCheckout": true,
      "TimeoutSeconds": 15
    }
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-consumer
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: consumer
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: consumer
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: consumer
        image: app/consumer:v1
        volumeMounts:
        # NOTE: Mounting full directory uses Kubelet atomic symlinks for live updates!
        # Do NOT use subPath if you want live file updates without restarting pods.
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /etc/app-config
          readOnly: true
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        configMap:
          name: app-dynamic-config
breakdown: Mounting the ConfigMap as a directory allows Kubelet to update the underlying ..data symlink atomically within ~60 seconds of ConfigMap edits, enabling zero-restart hot-reloads.
expectedOutput: Modifying app-dynamic-config updates /etc/app-config/appsettings.json inside the running container in real time without pod restarts.

title: Preserving Client Source IP with ExternalTrafficPolicy Local
whatThisCodeCovers: A LoadBalancer Service configured with externalTrafficPolicy: Local to prevent SNAT rewriting and preserve true client IP addresses for auditing and geofencing.
code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: public-web-ingress
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-scheme: "internet-facing"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  # CRITICAL: Local preserves original client IP and avoids extra inter-node hops
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  selector:
    app: public-nginx
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
    protocol: TCP
    name: http
  - port: 443
    targetPort: 8443
    protocol: TCP
    name: https
breakdown: Setting externalTrafficPolicy to Local instructs kube-proxy to bypass SNAT. Only nodes hosting healthy pods receive external traffic, exposing the client's actual IP to X-Forwarded-For.
expectedOutput: Application container logs display genuine client public IP addresses instead of cluster node private IP addresses.

title: Optimized NodeLocal DNSCache DaemonSet with CoreDNS Rewrites
whatThisCodeCovers: A NodeLocal DNSCache DaemonSet setup running a local caching agent on 169.254.20.10 to eliminate 5-second DNS timeouts and conntrack table saturation.
code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: node-local-dns
  namespace: kube-system
data:
  Corefile: |
    cluster.local:53 {
        errors
        cache {
            success 9984 30
            denial 9984 5
        }
        reload
        loop
        bind 169.254.20.10
        forward . __PILLAR__CLUSTER__DNS__ {
            force_tcp
        }
        prometheus :9253
        health 169.254.20.10:8080
    }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# runbooks/drain_node.sh
set -euo pipefail

NODE_NAME="$1"

echo "=== Step 1: Cordoning node ${NODE_NAME} (Halting new scheduling) ==="
kubectl cordon "${NODE_NAME}"

echo "=== Step 2: Checking PodDisruptionBudgets in cluster ==="
kubectl get pdb -A

echo "=== Step 3: Evicting workloads with safety thresholds ==="
kubectl drain "${NODE_NAME}" \
  --ignore-daemonsets \
  --delete-emptydir-data \
  --grace-period=60 \
  --timeout=5m \
  --skip-wait-for-delete-timeout=30

echo "=== Step 4: Maintenance ready. Node ${NODE_NAME} successfully drained. ==="
# Execute OS reboot / kernel patch here...

echo "=== Step 5: Returning node to schedulable pool ==="
kubectl uncordon "${NODE_NAME}"
breakdown: Prevents downtime during infrastructure maintenance: marks node unschedulable, invokes the eviction API honoring PDBs, ignores node-level DaemonSets, and uncordons once maintenance concludes.
expectedOutput: Pods migrate smoothly to other nodes with zero application downtime before the host undergoes OS reboot.

title: Disaster Recovery Script: etcdctl TLS Snapshot Backup Automation
whatThisCodeCovers: An automated bash backup script that creates a consistent point-in-time snapshot of the etcd database using mTLS certificates and validates database integrity.
code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/backup_etcd.sh
set -euo pipefail

TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
BACKUP_DIR="/var/backups/etcd"
BACKUP_FILE="${BACKUP_DIR}/etcd_snapshot_${TIMESTAMP}.db"

mkdir -p "${BACKUP_DIR}"

echo "=== Taking consistent point-in-time etcd snapshot ==="
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save "${BACKUP_FILE}" \
  --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key

echo "=== Verifying snapshot integrity ==="
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --write-out=table snapshot status "${BACKUP_FILE}"

echo "=== Compressing snapshot and syncing to encrypted S3 bucket ==="
gzip -c "${BACKUP_FILE}" > "${BACKUP_FILE}.gz"
aws s3 cp "${BACKUP_FILE}.gz" s3://company-k8s-disaster-recovery/cluster-prod/ --sse aws:kms

echo "=== etcd backup successfully completed and verified. ==="
breakdown: Uses ETCDCTL_API=3 to take a consistent snapshot of the B+ tree database using master certificates, verifies the hash table integrity, and uploads the compressed snapshot to cloud cold storage.
expectedOutput: A validated etcd snapshot saved and securely synced to S3 with a table displaying total keys and revision index.

title: Diagnostic Runbook: Remediating CrashLoopBackOff Exit Code 137 (OOMKilled)
whatThisCodeCovers: An SRE diagnostic workflow using kubectl, cAdvisor, and dmesg to diagnose and resolve Exit Code 137 Out-Of-Memory container termination.
code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# runbooks/diagnose_oom.sh
POD="$1"
NAMESPACE="$2"

echo "=== 1. Inspecting Termination Reason and Exit Code ==="
kubectl get pod "${POD}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" -o jsonpath='{range .status.containerStatuses[*]}{.name}{": Reason="}{.lastState.terminated.reason}{" ExitCode="}{.lastState.terminated.exitCode}{"\n"}{end}'

echo "=== 2. Tailing logs from crashed instance ==="
kubectl logs "${POD}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" --previous --tail=50

echo "=== 3. Inspecting configured memory requests vs limits ==="
kubectl get pod "${POD}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" -o jsonpath='{range .spec.containers[*]}{.name}{": requests.memory="}{.resources.requests.memory}{" limits.memory="}{.resources.limits.memory}{"\n"}{end}'

echo "=== 4. Checking node kernel dmesg for OOM-killer invocations ==="
NODE=$(kubectl get pod "${POD}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}')
echo "Pod was placed on node: ${NODE}"
# Inspect dmesg: dmesg -T | grep -i -E "oom-killer|killed process"
breakdown: Detects OOMKilled exit code 137, inspects preceding application memory logs, and compares configured memory limits against container runtime needs to right-size specifications.
expectedOutput: Pinpoints memory limit violations and outputs exact adjustments required for resources.limits.memory.

title: Diagnostic Runbook: Resolving ImagePullBackOff with Docker Registry Secrets
whatThisCodeCovers: A diagnostic script to triage ImagePullBackOff errors and bind docker-registry credentials to ServiceAccounts for automated private image authentication.
code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# runbooks/fix_image_pull.sh
set -euo pipefail

NAMESPACE="$1"
SECRET_NAME="enterprise-registry-creds"

echo "=== Step 1: Creating docker-registry secret in namespace ${NAMESPACE} ==="
kubectl create secret docker-registry "${SECRET_NAME}" \
  --namespace="${NAMESPACE}" \
  --docker-server="registry.company.internal" \
  --docker-username="$REGISTRY_USER" \
  --docker-password="$REGISTRY_TOKEN" \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

echo "=== Step 2: Patching default ServiceAccount to automatically inject secret ==="
kubectl patch serviceaccount default \
  -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
  -p '{"imagePullSecrets": [{"name": "'"${SECRET_NAME}"'"}]}'

echo "=== Step 3: Verified. All new pods in ${NAMESPACE} inherit credentials. ==="
breakdown: Creates a docker-registry secret and patches the namespace's default ServiceAccount, ensuring all workloads in the namespace automatically pull images from private registries without modifying individual Deployment specs.
expectedOutput: Pods previously stuck in ErrImagePull / ImagePullBackOff successfully authenticate and launch.

title: Diagnostic Runbook: Unblocking Pending Pods Trapped in Predicate Failures
whatThisCodeCovers: An automated diagnostic script identifying why Pods remain in Pending state, extracting scheduler predicate errors and cluster node capacity deficits.
code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# runbooks/triage_pending_pods.sh
set -euo pipefail

NAMESPACE="${1:-default}"

echo "=== Listing all Pending Pods in namespace '${NAMESPACE}' ==="
PENDING_PODS=$(kubectl get pods -n "${NAMESPACE}" --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}')

if [ -z "${PENDING_PODS}" ]; then
  echo "No pending pods found."
  exit 0
fi

for POD in ${PENDING_PODS}; do
  echo "---------------------------------------------------------"
  echo "POD: ${POD}"
  echo "Scheduler Failure Reason:"
  kubectl get events -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
    --field-selector "involvedObject.name=${POD},reason=FailedScheduling" \
    --sort-by='.metadata.creationTimestamp' \
    -o custom-columns=TIME:.metadata.creationTimestamp,MESSAGE:.message | tail -n 2
done

echo "---------------------------------------------------------"
echo "=== Cluster Allocatable vs Capacity Summary ==="
kubectl describe nodes | grep -A 8 "Allocated resources:"
breakdown: Parses FailedScheduling events to instantly tell the engineer whether the issue is Insufficient CPU/Memory, untolerated taints, or unbound PersistentVolumeClaims.
expectedOutput: Diagnostic summary pinpointing predicate failure causes (e.g. '0/12 nodes available: 12 Insufficient cpu').

title: ResourceQuota & LimitRange Enforcing Fair Share Compute Across Namespaces
whatThisCodeCovers: Enterprise multi-tenancy manifests setting hard namespace compute ceilings with ResourceQuota and mandating default CPU/RAM requests with LimitRange.
code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: default-limits
  namespace: development
spec:
  limits:
  - default: # Default limits if omitted by developer
      cpu: "500m"
      memory: "512Mi"
    defaultRequest: # Default requests if omitted
      cpu: "100m"
      memory: "128Mi"
    max:
      cpu: "2000m"
      memory: "2Gi"
    type: Container
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: compute-quota
  namespace: development
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "10"
    requests.memory: "20Gi"
    limits.cpu: "20"
    limits.memory: "40Gi"
    pods: "30"
    services.loadbalancers: "1"
breakdown: LimitRange injects default CPU/memory requests if developers omit them, preventing unconstrained containers. ResourceQuota bounds total namespace footprint, preventing noisy neighbor starvation.
expectedOutput: Development namespace caps total resource usage to 10 CPUs / 20Gi RAM, automatically injecting default container sizes.

title: Secret Encryption at Rest via kube-apiserver KMS v2 Provider
whatThisCodeCovers: The kube-apiserver EncryptionConfiguration manifest implementing envelope encryption with external cloud KMS (AWS KMS / HashiCorp Vault) for Secrets stored in etcd.
code:
apiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1
kind: EncryptionConfiguration
resources:
  - resources:
      - secrets
      - configmaps
    providers:
      # 1. Primary: Cloud KMS v2 Provider (Envelope Encryption)
      - kms:
          apiVersion: v2
          name: aws-kms-provider
          endpoint: unix:///var/run/kmsplugin/socket.sock
          timeout: 3s
      # 2. Secondary fallback (Read existing AES-CBC secrets during migration)
      - aescbc:
          keys:
            - name: legacy-key
              secret: c2VjcmV0IGlzIGEgMzItYnl0ZSBzdHJpbmc=
      # 3. Identity (Plaintext fallback for unencrypted legacy objects)
      - identity: {}
breakdown: Configures kube-apiserver to encrypt Secret values before writing to etcd using KMS envelope encryption. If the etcd disk is stolen, the raw database contains only unreadable ciphertext.
expectedOutput: etcd stores Secrets as ciphertext encrypted with dynamic DEKs rotated and protected by cloud hardware KMS.

title: Ephemeral Containers (kubectl debug) for Live Production Troubleshooting
whatThisCodeCovers: Using ephemeral debug containers to attach interactive troubleshooting toolkits (curl, tcpdump, gdb) to live distroless production pods without restarting them.
code:
# 1. Attach an ephemeral debugging container into a live distroless pod
$ kubectl debug -it payment-api-78f99-z9k12 \
    --image=nicolaka/netshoot \
    --target=payment-api \
    -n production

# Inside the netshoot ephemeral container:
# You now share the pod's network namespace and process namespace!
$ tcpdump -i eth0 -nn -s0 -v port 8080
$ curl -v http://localhost:8080/healthz
$ strace -p 1 -f -e trace=network

# 2. Alternatively, copy a crashing pod with an interactive override
$ kubectl debug pod/crashing-pod-abc \
    --copy-to=debug-pod \
    --container=app \
    --sh
breakdown: Solves the dilemma of inspecting hardened distroless containers (which lack shells and package managers): dynamically injects a temporary debugging container into the pod's shared Linux namespaces.
expectedOutput: Instant interactive shell inside the production pod's network and process namespace with zero workload disruption.

title: PriorityClass Hierarchy: Critical System Workloads vs Batch Jobs
whatThisCodeCovers: Defining cluster-wide PriorityClass tiers with preemption policies to guarantee mission-critical microservices pre-empt low-priority batch jobs during capacity shortages.
code:
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: mission-critical-service
value: 1000000000 # High priority
globalDefault: false
description: "Core revenue-generating microservices (payment, checkout)."
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: background-batch-job
value: 1000 # Low priority
globalDefault: false
preemptionPolicy: Never # Never pre-empt other workloads
description: "Non-critical batch data processing."
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-engine
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 4
  template:
    spec:
      priorityClassName: mission-critical-service
      containers:
      - name: payment
        image: payment:v2
breakdown: When nodes reach 100% capacity, kube-scheduler evicts low-priority batch jobs (value: 1000) to ensure mission-critical service pods (value: 1000000000) schedule without delay.
expectedOutput: Mission-critical pods immediately pre-empt background jobs during node resource crunch.
